title: Purchase of Alaska: From Russian Exploration to Statehood
learningObjectives: Sequence Russian exploration, the 1859 offer, and the 1867 purchase and transfer of Alaska.
Explain how limited Russian settlement and external rivalries led to the sale and U.S. acquisition.
Trace post-purchase governance, gold discovery, and Alaska's path to statehood in 1959.

explanations.text: Russia maintained a small presence in Alaska despite early exploration, and strategic pressures reduced its interest.

evidence.quote: Defeat in the Crimean War further reduced Russian interest in this region.
and permanent Russian settlers in Alaska never numbered more than four hundred

explanations.text: Diplomatic offers in 1859 and renewed negotiations after the Civil War led to the 1867 agreement and formal transfer.

evidence.quote: Russia offered to sell Alaska to the United States in 1859
on March 30, 1867, agreed to a proposal from Russian Minister in Washington, Edouard de Stoeckl, to purchase Alaska for $7.2 million

explanations.text: After purchase, Alaska was governed under federal systems until mining laws, gold discovery, and finally statehood established its modern status.

evidence.quote: the United States constituted a civil government in 1884
Alaska became a state on January 3, 1959

events.label: Peter the Great dispatches Vitus Bering

evidence.quote: Beginning in 1725, when Russian Czar Peter the Great dispatched Vitus Bering to explore the Alaskan coast
Russia had a keen interest in this region, which was rich in natural resources and lightly inhabited
Russia offered to sell Alaska to the United States in 1859
on March 30, 1867, agreed to a proposal from Russian Minister in Washington, Edouard de Stoeckl, to purchase Alaska for $7.2 million
Alaska was formally transferred to the United States on October 18, 1867
the United States constituted a civil government in 1884
when a major gold deposit was discovered in the Yukon in 1896
Alaska became a state on January 3, 1959
